title: a gate's log directory under tmp/ is given an ignore file in a repository git refuses to read, a directory the project tracks included, because the refusal is read as no repository
body:
## Problem

0157 writes `*` into `tmp/<command>/.gitignore` before a gate's first log lands, and never into a directory git tracks. `_gate_out_ignore_file` (lib/runlog) asks `git ls-files` whether the directory is tracked. When that fails it asks `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, and only if that succeeds does it say "git could not say whether <dir> is tracked" and write nothing. When both fail it takes the tree for one with no repository and returns the file to write, without a word.

A repository git refuses to read fails both. Git refuses a repository owned by another user, reporting dubious ownership unless `safe.directory` names it, and `git_readonly` sets no `safe.directory`, rightly: a repository git does not trust is not one devbin should read. So the refusal is read as no repository, the file lands in a directory the project tracks, and `*` there hides every file the project adds to it afterwards. That is the harm the function's own comment names. runlog.bats's arm for the case, "a git that cannot say whether a directory is tracked gives it no .gitignore, and says so (0157)", gives "a repository owned by someone else" as its example, but its fake git fails `ls-files` alone and answers `rev-parse`, so the case it names is not the case it drives.

## Measured (cc, 2026-10-07, on d7f2ed13, git 2.56.0)

A scratch repository with a tracked file in `tmp/reports/`, driven with `GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1`, git's own switch for treating a repository as another user's. `git_readonly` passes it through: it is not among `git rev-parse --local-env-vars`.

- `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` and `git ls-files` both exit 128 with "detected dubious ownership".
- `_gate_out_ignore_file <proj>/tmp/reports` prints the path and returns 0, with nothing on stderr, and `gate_out_ignore` writes `*` there at rc 0, with nothing on stderr.
- A file the project then adds to `tmp/reports/` is missing from `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`; with the ignore file moved away, the same status reads `?? tmp/reports/new.txt`.
- Controls: with git answering, `_gate_out_ignore_file` prints nothing and returns 1, the directory being tracked. With the arm's fake, `ls-files` failing and `rev-parse` answering, it says "git could not say whether <dir> is tracked, so it is given no .gitignore" and returns 1.

## Fix

Tell "no repository" from "a repository git will not answer for" without asking git to trust it. When `ls-files` fails, look for a `.git`, file or directory, at the project root or above it, where git's own discovery looks. Where there is one, say that git could not say what is tracked and write nothing; only a tree with no `.git` above it gets the file unannounced. The arm drives the real refusal with `GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1`, beside the fake it has, so the case it names is a case it runs.

## Done when

1. In a repository git refuses to read, a gate's log directory is given no ignore file and the run says why, held by an arm driven with `GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1` that is red on the base.
2. A tree with no repository above it still gets the file, and the arm's fake still draws its line.
3. It ships in the next release.

## Resolution

Landed at 79a06fd4 on a green full suite (vc's, 2210 of 2210 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261007-0923). `_gate_out_ignore_file` asks the filesystem whether a repository is there, through `git_marker_above` in lib/helpers, where it asked `git rev-parse`, and writes the ignore file only on its plain no. When `git ls-files` fails and a `.git` -- a directory, a gitfile, or a link -- sits at the project root or above it, the gate's log directory gets no ignore file, and the run says that git could not say what is tracked, with git's own first line on the warning; for a repository git refuses to read, that line names the dubious ownership. Only a tree with no `.git` above it gets the file unannounced. The test harness refuses a TMPDIR with a `.git` above it by name, as it already refused one inside a checkout. Held by two runlog.bats arms driven with GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 (a refused repository with a tracked and an untracked directory; a repository above the root, and a worktree's gitfile) and a helpers.bats arm for the helper's three answers, all red on the base; 12 mutants, 11 killed and 1 equivalent.

Known limits: the walk does not stop at GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES or a filesystem boundary, so a `.git` beyond either still counts, and a directory that is itself a bare repository counts as none. Where git is not on PATH, a repository's log directories now get no ignore file, and the run says so at each gate. fleet's seam_committed and five other readers still tell a refused repository from an absent one their own way, or not at all.
